cable-mill.name: Cable Mill and Cades Cove Visitor Center

itineraries.title: One day in the Smokies: across the ridge
itineraries.summary: A first visit that crosses the park on Newfound Gap Road, with the high ridge in the middle of the day and a waterfall walk that replaces the closed Laurel Falls.
itineraries.season: Built for April to Nov. 29, when Kuwohi Road and Roaring Fork are open. Winter swaps are given at each stop that closes.

plan.label: Day 1
plan.theme: Sugarlands to the state line and back

stops.text: Buy your parking tag here if you do not have one, check the closures board, and walk the short nature trail behind the building.
Drive Newfound Gap Road up to the state line. The overlook has the Rockefeller Memorial and an Appalachian Trail crossing. Expect it to be much colder and windier than town.
stops.status: Open year-round, closes for snow and ice

stops.text: Take Kuwohi Road out to the park's highest point. The paved walk to the tower is short but steep.
stops.swap: From Nov. 30 to spring the road is closed. Drive down to Elkmont and walk Little River Trail toward Huskey Branch Falls instead.

stops.text: Walk past the restored cabins of the old Elkmont community and follow Little River Trail upstream. The park suggests this walk while Laurel Falls is closed.
Loop the one-way Roaring Fork Motor Nature Trail past old homesteads and the Place of a Thousand Drips, then come out at the edge of Gatlinburg.
stops.status: Open Apr 17 to Nov 29 (2026). No buses, trailers or motor homes.
stops.swap: In winter, walk the Gatlinburg Trail from Sugarlands instead. It is one of two park trails that allow dogs.

itineraries.title: Two days on the quiet side: Cades Cove and Elkmont
itineraries.summary: Two slower days based in Townsend, built around Cades Cove at first light, with the Foothills Parkway for sunset and a history walk at Elkmont.
itineraries.season: Works all year. Abrams Falls Trail was closed through Sept. 30, 2026, so confirm it has reopened before you plan on it.

stops.text: Start the one-way loop as early as you can. Fog in the fields and deer, turkeys and bears are most likely early. Use pullouts only and stay in your car around bear jams.
stops.status: Open year-round. Car-free on Wednesdays May 6 to Sept 30 (2026).

stops.text: Stop midway at the Cable Mill and visitor center for the historic buildings and restrooms.
Drive back out and turn up Tremont Road for a quiet streamside walk and the small visitor center at the institute.
Drive the Foothills Parkway for open ridge views and walk up to the Look Rock tower before sunset.
Walk the restored cabins of the Elkmont historic district, then follow Little River Trail toward Huskey Branch Falls.
stops.status: Open. Access is limited during the late-May firefly event.

stops.text: Continue along Little River Road to Sugarlands for the exhibits and film, and pick up the Junior Ranger book if you have children.

itineraries.title: Three days across both states
itineraries.base: Townsend, then Cherokee or Bryson City
itineraries.summary: Cades Cove on the Tennessee side, the ridge crossing on the second day, and the North Carolina side for elk and waterfalls. This replaces the older plan that used Laurel Falls on day one.
itineraries.season: Days one and three work all year. Day two uses Kuwohi Road, which is open Apr 1 to Nov 29 (2026); a winter swap is given.

stops.text: Drive the Cades Cove Loop early, when fog sits in the fields and deer, turkeys and bears are most often seen from the car.
stops.status: Open year-round. Car-free on Wednesdays May 6 to Sept 30 (2026).

stops.text: Walk the Cable Mill area and stop at the visitor center.
Finish on the Foothills Parkway at Look Rock.

plan.label: Day 2
plan.theme: Over the ridge to North Carolina

stops.text: Check closures at Sugarlands before you cross the ridge.
Stop at the state line overlook on Newfound Gap Road.
stops.status: Open year-round, closes for snow and ice

stops.text: Walk up to the Kuwohi tower on the park's highest point.
stops.swap: In winter, walk the Kephart Prong Trail on the North Carolina side instead, past the remains of an old Civilian Conservation Corps camp.

stops.text: Walk the flat paths of the Mountain Farm Museum beside Oconaluftee Visitor Center. Nearby Mingus Mill is temporarily closed.
Watch for elk in the fields near the visitor center as the light drops. Stay at least 25 yards away.

plan.label: Day 3
plan.theme: North Carolina side: waterfalls or elk

stops.text: Walk the Deep Creek loop past Juney Whank, Tom Branch and Indian Creek falls, an easy-to-moderate walk the park suggests while Laurel Falls is closed. Rocks by the water are slick.
If you base in Maggie Valley instead, spend the day in Cataloochee Valley for elk at dawn or dusk and old frame buildings. The road in is narrow and partly gravel, so leave in daylight.
stops.status: Valley open year-round. Several trails damaged by Hurricane Helene.
